On Saturday, May 23, 2015 at 3:40:17 AM UTC-4, Nadine Gibson wrote:
I am at a loss of what to do to get STAN to install. I have tried everything that I can think of. I am not well versed in C++. I have R version 3.2.0 (2015-04-16) -- "Full of Ingredients" and Rtools 3.3 installed. I have a Windows 7 operating system. All packages are also in the most updated form.

I don't think that script will install at the moment due to the new version of BH. You could do it if you have the devtools package installed with

devtools::install_url("http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/BH/BH_1.55.0-3.tar.gz")
devtools::install_url("https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.6.0/rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz")
library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast")

Ben

messages.author: 7cdcdc7f4b092431
messages.subject: Re: ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rstan'
parts:
Success! Thank you so much. 

For anyone else who is having this problem: You need to make sure that the most current version of BH isn't installed with rstan as a dependency.
devtools::install_url("http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/BH/BH_1.55.0-3.tar.gz")

devtools::install_url("https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.6.0/rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz",dependencies = FALSE)
library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast")

- Nadine

  • downgrading to BH 1.55 allows the installation of rstan ;

HTH,

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rstan'
parts:
Yes, the problem is primarily related to the compilation of Stan.

Boost 1.58 broke backward compatibility in their lazy evaluation
library Fusion, which is used heavily in the Spirit Qi parser.

I've modified our parser code to match 1.58, with the consequence
that it no longer works with Boost versions before 1.56 (previous Stan was
at 1.55 to match BH before it changed). It's passing tests on the Mac,
but not on Windows. Here's the pull request, which references the branch:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/1460

It's a holiday weekend here in NY, but we'll get this sorted out on the Stan
C++ side later this week. A patch or updated version of RStan should follow.

Sorry the R library compatibility has been a problem. We weren't
anticipating an update of BH, which skipped 1.56 and 1.57 updates,
but we should've been ready with compatible code for existing Boost
releases.

- Bob

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rstan'
parts:
First of all, thanks for good suggestions.

It looks like that even in some academic environments install_url is not working properly.  Thus the following sequence brought me back to the working state:
download BH from http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/BH/BH_1.55.0-3.tar.gz
download rstan from https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.6.0/rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz

install.packages ("devtools")
library (devtools)
devtools::install_local ("c:/Tools/BH.zip")
install.packages (inline)
library (inline)
install.packages ("RcppEigen")
library (RcppEigen)
devtools::install_local ("c:/Tools/rstan.zip", dependencies = FALSE)

Thanks,
Linas
